role: Get-Me-Back breadcrumb model (BreadcrumbFix, BreadcrumbTrail) and the file-backed store for the one active trail (active.json) plus a newest-first archive of up to 50 trails (archive.json) in the App Group 'Breadcrumbs' directory.
types: BreadcrumbFix: struct — one Codable GPS fix (time, lat/lon, h-accuracy, optional altitude/course/speed)
BreadcrumbTrail: struct — Codable trail: startedAt, origin fix, ordered fixes, optional label and resolved origin label
BreadcrumbStore: final class @unchecked Sendable — serial-queue JSON persistence of active trail and archive
toplevel: BreadcrumbFix/BreadcrumbTrail use synthesized Codable/Equatable; files are JSON with iso8601 dates and sortedKeys. `static let shared` is created lazily on first access via the private init. Header comments (lines 127-140) describe active vs archive vs auto-imported workout trails (WorkoutRecorder+Context.swift:475 calls archive).

flags.text: No test in EmuquTests references BreadcrumbStore, BreadcrumbTrail or BreadcrumbFix: persistence, migration, the corrupt-archive refusal and the 50-trail cap are unverified.

flags.text: clear() runs unconditionally after archive(), but archive() returns without writing when archive.json is present-but-unreadable (decodeArchive nil), when encoding fails, or when the write fails; the active trail is then deleted anyway, so "Clear" in Get Me Back permanently loses it — the very loss the decodeArchive comment says the refusal prevents.

Synchronously reads and decodes archive.json as [BreadcrumbTrail] (newest first); returns [] when the file cannot be read and [] with an error log when decode fails.

flags.text: A present-but-unreadable archive (I/O error or before first unlock) returns [] with no log, unlike decodeArchive which distinguishes it; AI facts then tell the user they have no past trails.

loadArchive re-implements the read+decode of archive.json that decodeArchive already does, with different failure semantics (read failure -> [] silently here, -> nil there), so the two readers of the same file disagree on what an unreadable archive means.
